hints.title: Overlapping Prefix Segmentation Obstacle
hints.text: A prefix of the string might match multiple dictionary words of different lengths. If an early match leads to a dead end, backtracking naively takes exponential time. How can you mark which prefix lengths can be formed so later segments only build on validated prefixes?

hints.title: Prefix Decomposition Invariant
hints.text: A string prefix of length i can be segmented if and only if there exists a valid segmented prefix of length j < i such that the substring between j and i is in the dictionary.

hints.title: Boolean Reachability Array Procedure
hints.text: Create a boolean array of size n + 1 with index 0 set to true and all others false. Iterate each ending index i from 1 to n. For each starting index j from 0 to i, if index j is true and the substring from j to i exists in the dictionary set, mark index i as true and break early. Return the value at index n.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: length of string s (1 <= N <= 300)
M: number of words in dictionary
L: maximum length of word in dictionary
complexity.notes: Substring slicing and set lookup takes O(L) time across O(N^2) index pairs.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Brute-force recursive backtracking explores 2^N segmentations on inputs like s="aaaaab", words=["a", "aa", "aaa"].
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: A 1D boolean reachability array of size N + 1 avoids exponential recursion with minimal O(N) space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Using a hash set for O(1) dictionary lookups, correct base case dp[0]=True, 1-indexed DP alignment.
